 Judgment

This appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (the Act) has been filed by the claim petitioner in O.P.(MV) No.445 of 2017 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
Ottapalam, (the Tribunal), aggrieved by the amount of compensation granted by Award dated 18/11/2019.
The respondents herein are the respondents in the petition.
In this appeal, the parties and the documents will be referred to as described in the original petition.

2. According to the claim petitioner, on 03/01/2017 at about 02:00 p.m., while he was riding motorcycle bearing registration no.KL-51/E-2668 through Kulappully-Koonathara road and when he reached the place by name Parakkuttikkavu temple, car bearing registration No.KL-09/AD-5371 driven by the first respondent in a rash and negligent manner, knocked him down, as a result of which he 2025:KER:74027 sustained grievous injuries.
3. The first respondent/driver and the second respondent/owner remained ex parte.

sentences.text: 4. The third respondent/insurer filed written statement denying the policy of the offending vehicle.
5. The fourth respondent/insurer filed written statement admitting the policy but denying negligence on the part of the first respondent/driver of the offending car.
The age, occupation and income were disputed.
It was also contended that the amount claimed was excessive.
6. Before the Tribunal, PW1 was examined and Exts.A1 to A8 were marked on the side of the claim petitioner.
No evidence was produced by the respondents.

7. The Tribunal on consideration of the oral and documentary evidence and after hearing both sides,
found negligence on the part of the first respondent/driver of the offending car resulting in the incident and hence awarded an amount of 3,66,660/- together with interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of petition till realisation along 2025:KER:74027 with proportionate costs.
Aggrieved by the Award, the claim petitioner has come up in appeal.
8. The only point that arises for consideration in this appeal is whether there is any infirmity in the findings of the Tribunal calling for an interference by this Court.
9. Heard both sides.
10. The award of compensation by the Tribunal under the following heads is challenged by the claim petitioner- Notional income
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioner that the latter, a manual labourer, was earning 15,000/- per month.

However, the Tribunal fixed the notional income at 8,000/-, which is quite low going by the dictum in Ramachandrappa v.
Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Co. Ltd, (2011) 13 SCC 236.
10.1.

sentences.text: In the light of the dictum in Ramachandrappa (Supra) the notional income is fixed as 11,000/-.
2025:KER:74027 Loss of earnings 11.

The materials on record show that the claim petitioner sustained the following injuries:
"Crush injury to the right foot, amputation 2nd, 3rd, 4th toes of right foot distal half,
multiple laceration to forefoot with medial two tarso metatarsal joints dislocated and heel pad avulsion."
He was hospitalized for a period of 5 days.
In all probability, he might have been unable to work for a period of 8 months.

Hence, he can be awarded compensation of - 11,000/-x8 months =
88,000/-.
Compensation for pain and suffering 12.
In the light of the injuries sustained, I find that an amount of 60,000/- as claimed under this head would be just and reasonable .

In the result, the appeal is allowed by enhancing the compensation by a further amount of 1,52,760/- (total compensation =5,19,420/- that is, 3,66,660/-

granted in appeal) with interest at the rate of 8% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization and proportionate costs.
